material_items.notes: FileManager owns path-based OpenFile while Contracts owns OpenSubject identity routing and route_target normalization.
The shared buffer authority, typed mutation sources, save authority, embedded document pane sharing, and dirty/on-disk state are canonical.
Default open target is the active focused editor group; target_group is placement only and not route identity.
MVP supports exactly one floating editor window, with detached surfaces retaining the same identity and synchronized buffers/tabs.
Soft warning at 10000 lines and hard open cap at 5 MB are explicit.
Open tabs, active tab, scroll/cursor, transient states, layout, and route identity are separated.
Preview-generated source patches are bounded shared-buffer mutations; derivative preview/source mode remains FileManager and Final GUI canon.
Current owner docs cover degraded and unavailable index, LSP, search, and remote states more explicitly than the research ledger.
UI dispatches commands and consumes service projections; native workspace services own buffers, LSP, search, remote, routing, and persistence.

INV-022 now states watchers and provider streams are invalidation signals; missed, coalesced, overflowed, or untrusted events trigger bounded reconciliation or rescan through the owning service before projections are current.
INV-022 now states Git/SCM subprocess work is not an editor or UI hot-path dependency; SCM refreshes are coalesced, budgeted, projected, and revalidated before mutation.
Rust core owns editor and workspace state; Slint surfaces are consumers, not the state owner.
Workspace layout, editor tabs, route identity, and per-view line/range/subview state remain separated.
Remote editing is MVP FileManager scope; remote terminal and run/debug availability are separate runtime-surface capabilities and cannot be implied by editing a remote file.
The current canon retires browser_panel labels to compatibility aliases and removes optional/future gap framing from the FileManager owner sections.
Durable research/process context is retained only as source-lineage memory and was not transferred into product canon.
